records.summary: Patriots OC Josh McDaniels says the Super Bowl protection failure against Seattle was a major lesson after Drake Maye was sacked six times. The rematch features a healthier Will Campbell, Jared Wilson back at his natural center position, and free-agent addition Alijah Vera-Tucker, while Seattle returns most of the front that created the prior pressure problems. McDaniels also says Maye enters with materially more system knowledge after a second full offseason. This modestly improves New England's protection/continuity outlook versus the Super Bowl baseline but does not imply a side or total.
records.direction: improved Patriots protection/continuity relative to prior Seattle matchup, still tested by returning Seattle front

records.summary: The 49ers and Rams are using materially different preparation strategies for the Melbourne opener. San Francisco arrived a full week before kickoff and is actively acclimating to local time with structured sleep/recovery protocols; Kyle Shanahan said players needed several days to feel normal. Los Angeles plans to arrive Thursday, roughly one day before the Friday-morning local kickoff after a 16-plus-hour flight, intentionally avoiding full acclimation. Sleep-performance specialists interviewed by the Chronicle say the Rams may benefit from playing near their U.S. body-clock performance window, but face greater immediate travel-fatigue, dehydration, sleep-loss and freshness risk; the 49ers reduce immediate travel fatigue but must manage jet lag. This is situational matchup context only, not a side/total wager.
records.direction: 49ers better acclimated; Rams retain body-clock-window argument but carry higher immediate travel-fatigue risk
records.construction_detail: Australia travel/acclimation contrast; no betting construction stated
